summary: settleRoomWithin (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/service.go:1214) keeps the offsets of its first render of `read` (service.go:1428, renderTreeWithOffsets instead of renderTree) and reuses that markdown, those offsets and that error at service.go:1594 only when `versioned == read && !reconciliation.changedTree()`; otherwise it renders `versioned` as today. changedTree() is a new settlementReconciliation method (ask_blocks.go) returning len(r.repairs) > 0 || len(r.rewrites) > 0, because reconcileAskBlocks changes the tree in place and records every change there. The ranking's X5 condition (len(slots)==0) is wrong in two cases: a repair the live write did not need (applySuppressed returns no slot, service.go:425-427, while `read` was repaired in memory) and a stamp that minted nothing (reconciled replaced by the stamp's tree, service.go:1467). The INFRA-512 architect agreed to this condition on 2026-10-27 at 15:10Z.
tasks: 1. Code: service.go:1428 and :1594, plus changedTree() in ask_blocks.go with a doc comment, plus a comment stating the invariant (read is a private copy that only reconcileAskBlocks changes, each change recorded). Superseded path, closureChangedMarkdown and withholdAnswers' renders stay unchanged.

2. Two permanent regression tests in the docs package: (a) a repair the room already holds (a peer wrote the same attributes in afterSettleReconcile, observer held with beforeObserveUpdate) is versioned as repaired, and its block rows equal the offsets of the room's rendering; (b) a stamp that minted nothing (another writer stamped the ids in afterSettleRead) versions the stamp's tree's block ids. Negative control: both fail under the ranking's len(slots)==0 condition. Then the whole docs package, ./internal/dispatch/... ./cmd/dispatch/... and go vet, against Postgres 17 + pgvector (DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL).

3. A throwaway real-size equivalence harness (not committed: the repository is public): at least 20 real LINUX specs from dispatch doc-read (the largest at 660 KB, plus LINUX-43, -129 and -364) under $TMPDIR, one settlement on each path (plain edit, repaired ask, stamp, render refusal if it can be built), with a dump of version number, markdown sha256, block rows, excerpts and document token at base (git archive) and at head. The diff must be empty. Negative control under the ranking's condition.

4. Merge rule on the architect's replay (dispatch://INFRA-647 comment db51d4c0): the tools tarball and replay-inputs.tar.gz parts 00-10 checked with sha256, Postgres 17 + pgvector on :55432, NATS, fakelistener; base and head built with GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/dispatch; for each run, a fresh restore of run/seeded.dump, then BIN=<binary> GOMAXPROCS=2 tools/run-dispatch.sh, then tools/drive.sh <side>-<n> 0.3 1 27 8, alternating base and head three times each. Rule A: max(head CPU-s) < min(base CPU-s). Otherwise, when G (half the base W14 CPU-seconds, from the Appendix A command) is below the spread, rule B: the median head settleRoomWithin cumulative share is at least W14_base_share/4 below the median base share. Also quote the -lines -peek split of renderTreeWithOffsets under settleRoomWithin. If neither rule holds: a write-up on INFRA-512 and a report to the architect, no merge. If INFRA-639's replay is runnable when measuring, use it with the same inputs instead.
5. Docs: one sentence in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md's settlement paragraph (~line 69); a ### Changed entry under [Unreleased] in packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md.

6. PR with Dispatch: INFRA-647 and the pr-body template; E2E (implementer) = task 4 with negative controls from tasks 2 and 3; ce-simplify-code once; Production line after the merge (Cloud Monitoring CPU + live profile once a build containing the merge runs, pending deploy until then).

specDepartures.spec: Outcome: Fix X5 ... Render once. X5 (cited by the spec) reuses the first render when no closure or repair wrote anything (len(slots) == 0 and versioned is reconciled).
specDepartures.plan: Reuses the first render only when versioned == read and the reconciliation recorded no repair and no rewrite. Settlements that stamped (even with nothing minted) or repaired the tree in memory render the version again, as today.
specDepartures.evidence: reconcileAskBlocks changes `read` in place (ask_blocks.go:85, :98/:786, ask_block_text.go:322) and applySuppressed returns no slot when the live write changed nothing (service.go:425-427); a stamp that mints nothing replaces reconciled with its own tree without a slot (service.go:1467). Under X5's condition those versions would differ from today's. The INFRA-512 architect agreed at 15:10Z.
